sources.title: BDUK GigaHubs Evaluation: Process Review
facts: Published 26 June 2026 as a process review of GigaHubs delivered through Project Gigabit.
The publication contains summary, full review, theory of change, annex and interview framework documents.
The review assesses how programme design, delivery partners and market developments shaped rural public-building connectivity.

sources.title: GigaHubs Process Review Summary
facts: GigaHubs delivered about 1,200 Hub connections during 2021-26 through six projects.
The summary reports 5,670 BDUK Hubs delivered as of September 2025.
Evidence combines BDUK management data with interviews across government, local authorities, suppliers and sites.

sources.title: GigaHubs Process Review Theory of Change
facts: The document records the programme theory of change used by the GigaHubs process review.
It separates programme inputs and delivery processes from outcomes and wider effects.
It is evaluation evidence and not a current premises-level service record.

sources.title: GigaHub Process Review Annex
facts: The annex supplies supporting detail for the GigaHubs process review.
Its role is methodological and contextual rather than a live coverage dataset.
Annex evidence must remain distinct from current orderability or exact UPRN truth.

sources.title: Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan
sources.lines: publication page and detailed HTML plan
facts: The plan covers evaluation of Project Gigabit, GIS and the Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme.
It defines process, impact and economic evaluation activities.
Connectivity outcomes are scheduled later than initial baselining, so plan milestones are not current service evidence.

sources.title: BDUK Hubs Evaluation Plan
facts: Published 15 August 2025 and covering evaluation activity from 2024 to 2027.
The intervention connects remote schools, GP surgeries and libraries to gigabit-capable broadband.
The plan distinguishes earlier Rural Gigabit Connectivity Hubs from Project Gigabit GigaHubs.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network Evaluation Plan
facts: Published 15 August 2025 as the recommended approach to the full SRN evaluation.
BDUK commissioned Ipsos UK and partners to undertake the evaluation.
An evaluation plan does not establish current mobile coverage at a parcel or address.

sources.title: LFFN Wave 1 Interim Evaluation Schools Project
facts: Published 17 October 2022 as an interim evaluation of LFFN Wave One schools projects.
The Public Sector Buildings Upgrade aimed to provide schools with gigabit-capable connections.
COVID-19 affected delivery and changed the timing and interpretation of the interim assessment.

sources.title: Evaluation of BDUK Gigabit Vouchers: Initial Impacts and Benefits
facts: Published 30 August 2022 and evaluates the GBVS and RGC voucher products.
It includes counterfactual analysis of coverage and download-speed impacts for vouchers issued in 2019 and 2020.
It also includes analysis of an early-2022 business beneficiary survey.

sources.title: Superfast Broadband Programme: Synthesis and process evaluation reports 2021
facts: The publication compiles key findings, synthesis, process and wellbeing reports completed in 2021.
It evaluates benefits and how effectively the Superfast Broadband Programme was delivered.
The publication builds on earlier 2018 and 2020 evaluations.

sources.title: Local Full Fibre Network Programme: Wave 1 – interim evaluation
facts: This is an interim evaluation of the first wave of the Local Full Fibre Network Programme.
It is programme-evaluation evidence rather than live premises coverage data.
Findings require preservation of project scope, evaluation period and counterfactual limitations.

sources.title: Superfast Broadband Programme - State Aid Evaluation Report 2020
facts: The report evaluates the Superfast Broadband Programme under its State aid framework.
Its evidence concerns programme effectiveness and compliance in the evaluated period.
Historical State aid findings cannot be promoted to current address-level availability.

sources.title: Evaluation of the SuperConnected Cities Programme
facts: The publication evaluates the SuperConnected Cities Programme.
Its scope is programme impact and delivery, not current nationwide broadband coverage.
Any geographic findings must retain the cities and dates used by the evaluation.

sources.title: Evaluation of the Economic Impact and Public Value of the Superfast Broadband Programme
facts: The report evaluates economic impact and public value associated with the Superfast Broadband Programme.
Impact estimates are evaluation outputs tied to methods and observation periods.
They are not evidence that a specific premises currently has an orderable service.
